sheets.title: World imageboard
sheets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a high quality anime art-of production design book sheet for MELOS GAME, stage 1-9 THE TRICKSTER PARADE. This is a proposed expanded design based on the actual existing game art, not a game screenshot.
Reference roles: provided theatre background is the environment/style reference; provided gremlin atlas is the established enemy identity reference; provided mouth gate and floor are prop style and shape language references. Preserve the existing world: a floating mechanical theatre city above peach clouds, ornate wooden opera balconies, coral lacquer, deep teal patina, brass gears, amber bulbs, marionette masks, red curtains, whimsical sinister comedy. Foreground devices have strong silhouettes, restrained ornament and clear working parts, soft atmospheric backgrounds. 2D hand-painted anime animation production artwork, expressive linework, gouache color, tactile painted wood and metal; no photorealism, no glossy 3D.
Print-like cream paper layout with disciplined spacing, small ink construction drawings and selective accent callouts. English text only, few large readable labels, no tiny fake prose, no Japanese, no watermark. Keep every important design fully within the page. Amber concentric target rings consistently identify SHOOTABLE mechanisms; cyan sketched platforms consistently identify the second player's DRAW ability. Avoid medieval castle battlements, generic spikes, combat weapons unrelated to theatre, or repeating a mouth and hammer across every scene.
Asset type: LANDSCAPE setting imageboard, approximately 3:2, a rich but legible art book double-page spread.
Main request: express a dangerous living theatre whose scenery becomes the route. Top 60% is a single large cinematic environmental vista. Foreground side-on stage promenade across floating opera buildings: smiling tooth gate at left; fly-tower with a suspended curtain and visible paired counterweights center-left; split parade paths around a round turning stage at center; concertina bellows bridge above cloud gap center-right; a large sun-faced Ferris wheel with horizontal hanging theatre-box cabins at right. Small wind-up masked gremlins crowd the turning stage. A tiny navy-and-coral runner stands on a cyan drawn rescue platform to establish scale. Architecture from reference, purposeful new stage machines; visually open sky and route.
Bottom 40% has three clean inset concept panels: MASK GATE close-up retaining the reference grin; BACKSTAGE cross-section showing cable connecting a descending counterweight and rising curtain; SKY WHEEL close-up of cabin brake and loading ledge. Show restrained six-swatch palette coral, teal, brass, cream, sky, ink, plus simple floor edge construction sketch.
Text verbatim only: "THE TRICKSTER PARADE", "WORLD IMAGEBOARD", "MASK GATE", "BACKSTAGE", "SKY WHEEL", "DESIGN EXPLORATION". Composition should feel like a professional animation setting collection, not a poster collage.

Asset type: LANDSCAPE theatre machine setting sheet, 3:2, six numbered panels in two rows of three on cream paper.
Title "STAGE MACHINES". Subtitle "SHOOT / DRAW / CHANGE THE ROUTE". Each panel has ONE large device drawing plus a smaller action/result inset and sparse mechanical arrows; omit all other prose. Show actual useful visual cause and effect, not decorative props. Devices in strict reading order:
01 "MASK GATE": retain existing large teal coral smiling fang arch. A shot on its amber cheek latch unfolds the hinged lower jaw into a bridge, teeth fold down flush; show closed teeth and open flat bridge silhouettes.
02 "CURTAIN LIFT": heavy velvet coral curtain connects via overhead pulley cable to a broad teal brass counterweight platform. Shooting the amber latch raises the curtain but lowers the weight and changes upper/lower routes. Inset shows cyan drawn platform catching the small runner as scenery changes.
03 "PARADE TURNTABLE": circular theatre deck drawn side-view plus small overhead diagram. Amber clutch target changes the rotation, arrow flags distinguish two branching exits, gremlins move into a different lane. Show one oversized established red brass hammer at one exit as a secondary hazard, not main topic.
04 "ACCORDION BRIDGE": giant teal coral concertina bellows bridging a cloud gap. Several gremlins' visible weight compresses it, brass spring lock is shot, it expands and launches gremlins and runner upward; show compression→release arc to a cyan catch platform.
05 "FOLLOW SPOT": vintage brass theatrical lamp and motorized lens on balcony. Golden light cone shows a masked stagehand with visible strings as a hostile puppet; the unlit silhouette is disguised as an innocent stage prop. Two stable lamp directions, amber lens target, the hero moves using the lamp's state change.
06 "SKY WHEEL": Ferris wheel with hanging opera-box cabins. A shot on cabin brake locks a cabin horizontally at a boarding ledge, cyan drawn transfer platform connects cabins. Gremlins loading an opposite cabin alter wheel balance, large curved direction arrow. A small real red goal flag is on the upper-right exit balcony.
Only exact labels above and numerals 01-06. Consistent visible materials and functional hinges, no disconnected mechanical arrows, no duplicated devices, no gore.

Title "THE PARADE CAST". Subtitle "SILHOUETTE / EXPRESSION / BEHAVIOR". Five original theatre-world enemies in strict left-to-right order. Preserve identity family: coral theatre masks, golden slit eyes, teal wood-and-metal puppet bodies, brass joints and winding keys. All five should be unmistakably different in silhouette and stage behavior. Each column has one large full-body three-quarter painted model, a smaller side profile or expression, and a small action vignette near bottom. Include a thin shared scale baseline, no dense tiny text.
01 "WIND-UP GREMLIN": faithful established reference enemy, squat grin, curled coral mask, cream ruff, round teal torso, large brass back key. Vignette shows a packed running crowd compressing an accordion bridge.

04 "BALLOON HARLEQUIN": light hanging jester with diamond-pattern silk cape and three small buoyant teal/gold/coral stage balloons on distinct cords, carries a single heavy brass prop sandbag. Vignette shows one cut cord causing bag to fall toward a waiting gremlin group; clear cord and weight linkage.
05 "SHADOW MARIONETTE": tall segmented wooden stagehand with smiling white/coral porcelain mask, black visible puppet strings, teal panels, black velvet cloak. Lit hostile spread-arms pose plus an unlit folded stool-like prop form. Vignette shows a golden spotlight switching between two poses.
Expressive comedy and readable safe vs threatening poses, no realistic flesh/blood, no characters unrelated to theatre, no copy-paste silhouettes. All full bodies including stilt feet and balloons remain on page. Exact text above only plus 01-05. Label the sheet "DESIGN EXPLORATION".

Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: wide LANDSCAPE illustrated side-on stage map for an anime art-of setting book, approximately 2.4:1.
Title "1-9 / THE TRICKSTER PARADE". Subtitle "PROPOSED STAGE MAP". Map is a continuous side-view schematic across the middle 75% of the page, never a top-down world map. Readable high-detail miniature props, spacious white/cream sky, floating theatre balconies above clouds. Six distinctly numbered chapters left→right, two connected route heights, red enemy path arrows and cyan player route arrows. Show unbroken traversable paths via platforms, lift or shown launch arcs, no unexplained leaps through empty space. This is a spatial design concept, not an exact gameplay screenshot or engineering blueprint. Use large 01-06 bubbles above matching zones, short exact labels below.
01 "FALSE ENTRANCE": START ledge→smiling mask arch with lower jaw bridge across a small gap. A gold target dot on cheek. Behind it, upper balcony reachable by cyan drawn platform and lower promenade.
02 "BACKSTAGE": tall fly-tower counterweight lift. Raised curtain reveals two routes, a very tall stilt usher guards the high path, teal counterweight platform connects low and high lanes. Small checkpoint pennant after zone.
03 "PARADE CROSSING": round rotating deck junction with a drum major and a tightly packed wind-up gremlin parade. Two exit lanes. One theatrical coral-and-brass stunt cannon covers only lower exit, raised balcony bypass at upper exit. Arrows show turntable direction changes redirect crowd. Keep this zone around middle of map.
04 "ACCORDION GAP": concertina spring bridge spans a deep cloud gap, crowd weight compresses it. Clearly drawn upward launch arc lands on a cyan drawn rescue platform then upper ledge. Balloon harlequin hangs over the gap with sandbag cord. Small checkpoint pennant after zone.
05 "SPOTLIGHT GALLERY": two balconies with a brass follow spotlight, light cone exposes one shadow marionette puppet, unlit folded props on the alternate path. Amber lens target. Upper/lower passage reconnect on right.
06 "SKY WHEEL FINALE": large sun Ferris wheel is the rightmost main silhouette. Hanging opera-box cabins at different heights, brake targets, boarding platform, opposite cabin loaded with gremlins to show counterweight. Cyan transfer platform and arrows connect an upper cabin to final balcony bearing red real GOAL flag.
At bottom: a simple six-card tempo strip only numbered 01-06, each shows a tiny sketch corresponding to the matching zone above. Small legend exact text "PLAYER ROUTE", "ENEMY FLOW", "SHOOT TARGET". Text only exact labels from this prompt. No duplicate zones, no castle, no decorative arrow spaghetti, no typography on the main platforms.
Additional reference roles: the world imageboard establishes landscape; machine setting sheet establishes precise device families (including the turntable's stunt cannon); enemy modelsheet establishes five distinct enemy identities. Keep this map's devices and cast consistent with these sheets. The cannon is a secondary turntable-lane hazard, not a seventh zone. The illustrated turntable may use a small oblique inset, but the overall route remains side-on.
